scope: 384 archived call files hashed; all 240 final raw responses independently parsed and compared with recorded assessments; calculator selection and Decimal arithmetic independently checked for all finals; group counts compared with frozen summary. Initial lineage was independently verified in the preceding archive audit.

findings.name: no_peer_probability_error
findings.meaning: Correct task posterior was available in calculator content, but final reported probability differed by more than 1e-4. No arithmetic or raw-response parsing discrepancy found in this audit.

findings.name: no_peer_MAP_disagreement
findings.meaning: All three reported the correct posterior yet answered the lower-probability state under symmetric MAP decision loss.

findings.name: no_peer_MAP_disagreement_repeats_initial_answer
findings.meaning: One case differs from the initial answer, so initial-answer persistence alone cannot descriptively account for all three. Agreement is not evidence of a cognitive cause.

findings.name: simple_probability_fingerprints
findings.meaning: No baseline probability error exactly matches these three candidates within tolerance. These candidates are not exhaustive and do not rule out approximate arithmetic or context effects.

findings.name: output_field_order
findings.meaning: Field order was not experimentally crossed; it cannot be assigned a causal role from this batch.

measurement_design_limitation: The frozen prompt specified the probability target but only required answer to be 0 or 1. It did not explicitly instruct a symmetric-loss MAP decision or tie rule. Consequently MAP disagreement is a scored convention, not established violation of an explicit decision instruction. This qualification does not remove the independent 44/48 posterior capability failure.

prior_art.title: From Evidence to Belief: A Bayesian Epistemology Approach to Language Models
prior_art.relevance: Evidence type, response accuracy and elicited confidence need not change together. Their natural QA evidence perturbations differ from our exact synthetic probability task; no direct reproduction claim.

prior_art.title: ADVICE: Answer-Dependent Verbalized Confidence Estimation
prior_art.read_scope: Abstract, sections 3.1-3.2 excerpts and prompt templates
prior_art.relevance: Answer-dependent confidence is prior art, so generic answer/confidence disconnection is not automatically novel. Crucially their confidence in a selected answer differs from our P(Y=1); their desired answer dependence must not be imposed on our fixed-event probability.

proposed_design_changes_not_run: Make event probability and decision distinct: p_state_1 always refers to Y=1; answer maximizes expected accuracy with equal error costs. Explicitly define p=0.5 tie behavior.
Preserve raw answer and probability as separate outcomes. Any deterministic MAP decoder is a labeled external baseline, not a repaired model answer.
If authorized, isolate explicit decision instruction from output-field ordering; do not change both and attribute the result to one.
Before attributing a peer effect, retain within-batch no-peer reconsideration and fixed evidence/calculator controls. Do not infer the effect of own prior from its correlation with a final answer.

A return to the original DICE utility claim still requires strong deduplication controls, delayed-release ablation, second-model replication and natural-task evaluation. Interface correctness alone is not an algorithmic contribution.
